payload.report: A 33-year-old man with recent Johnson & Johnson vaccination presents with hemoptysis, abdominal pain, dyspnea, lethargy, hypotension, and low-grade fever without infectious symptoms. The vaccination history, prothrombotic risk, abdominal pain with hemodynamic compromise, and exclusion of localizing infection strongly support vaccine-associated VITT/TTS. Expert consensus refines this to VITT/TTS complicated by splanchnic vein thrombosis, which best explains the abdominal pain and hypotension. Pulmonary embolism/infarction remains a secondary consideration given respiratory symptoms, while acute infection/sepsis and thrombotic microangiopathy are less likely but not fully excluded. Confirmatory tests—anti-PF4 ELISA, serotonin release assay, platelet/coagulation studies, and contrast-enhanced CT—are still pending, so definitive confirmation is lacking. Nevertheless, the overall evidence favors VITT/TTS complicated by splanchnic vein thrombosis as the most probable unifying diagnosis.
